description:
FILED s473t4 (#1501 CHECK 1 round 1, 2026-09-13).  Census finding: `Undefined subroutine &main::todo_skip called` aborts a top-level form of t/uni/overload.t (1 row short).

perl's own t/test.pl:
    sub todo_skip {
        my $why = shift;
        my $n   = @_ ? shift : 1;
        for (1..$n) {
            _print "not ok $test # TODO & SKIP $why\n";
            $test = $test + 1;
        }
        local $^W = 0;
        last TODO;
    }
The TAP half is trivial in PCL's stub (perl-tests/t/test.pl already owns `_tap_line` and `curr_test`).  What is NOT trivial is `last TODO`: it exits a loop labelled TODO in the CALLER's frame -- perl allows it with a warning ("Exiting subroutine via last").  PCL's loop-control family (#1244/#1161/#1164, round s473e) closed the in-unit cases; the residue s473e named is "a direct named call into another compilation unit", which is exactly this shape.

Its sibling `_create_runperl` is a SEPARATE filing (#1585).

VALUE: 1 row in the companion population, so this is a filler, not a round.  It is filed because the census must not leave `undef-fn:main::todo_skip` UNEXPLAINED, and because it is a clean small test of the cross-frame `last LABEL` mechanism.


=== DONE (s484d, shipped; bars re-measured s486c on the rebased tree) ===

`todo_skip` added to the PCL test.pl stub.  uni/overload.t 184/8 -> 184/9:
193 rows = perl's 193, its row-shortfall entry to zero.

THE CROSS-FRAME HALF NEEDED NO WORK, and that is the finding: `last TODO` out
of the sub into the CALLER's labelled block WORKS in PCL today -- probed on
uni/overload.t's exact shape.  The s473e residue this task quoted ("a direct
named call into another compilation unit") is measured working, so no #1244
work was owed.

s486c, at the rebase: the blessed row for test **192** ("TODO & SKIP RT #3054")
LEFT `baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv` -- PCL now emits `not ok N # TODO & SKIP`
exactly as perl does and the row stops diverging.  Main had, in the meantime,
attributed BOTH of uni/overload.t's todo_skip rows to this task; test **193**
survives with different verbs (`not ok` / `ok`, where the blessed row said
`(missing)`), so its `#1584` cause was retired rather than carried forward --
the surviving divergence is PCL PASSING a row perl has as a TODO failure, which
this round did not measure and did not invent a cause for.  It is the one
causeless row this branch adds.

BARS on the combined tree (s486c, rebased onto main 4429126a): gate
`Result: PASS` 243 files / 8216 rows; full perl-tests sweep GATE clean,
0 new / 0 fixed, TOTAL passing 18681 = 18681 (+0), drops 5 = census.
Companion `--all --quick --jobs 2`: see the s486c record.
